replay.note: the advocates' outputs were replayed from an earlier run and not regenerated by this one: only the judge was called, so the figures here measure the judge's behaviour on fixed inputs and not the whole pipeline

ruling.explanation:
Both of you agree on the numbers; the only real question is how much of the driver's detour is excused. Here is the decision.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00104 (admissibility weight 1.0, no issues) measures this trip at 34.17 km against the booked optimal of 27.1 km on the trip record EV-TRIP-00104 (weight 1.0). POL-RD-01 requires the trace figure to govern over the rounded trip-record copy, and it gives an excess of 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal — above both the 20% and the 0.8 km establishment tests. A route deviation is therefore established, and the rider's POL-RD-01 claim is accepted. The same trace is clean for policy purposes: 283 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gap over 90 seconds and no jump over 500 m, so POL-RD-07 adds nothing and the deviation stands on the trace alone. The excess is not material (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so no POL-RD-06 uplift or driver-conduct referral arises.

WHAT IS EXCUSED. The driver is right that the LTA accident advisory ADV-20260716-007 (EV-ADVIS-00104-01, weight 1.0) applies, and I accept his POL-RD-03 claim in part. It names the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link, a segment the booked optimal route traverses; it was valid 20:02-21:35 and overlaps the trip by 53.1 minutes; and the trace leaves the PIE at Bedok North Ave 4 before the blocked stretch and rejoins on the AYE. But POL-RD-03 exonerates only up to its cap: min(7.07 km, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km. That leaves 2.17 km of the excess unexplained and chargeable.

WHY NOT A FULL REFUND. The rider claimed about $14, but 4.90 km of the 7.07 km detour is excused as genuine accident-avoidance, and the fare is METERED with quoted_fare_sgd null, so POL-RD-11 does not run and the refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. Against the closure-adjusted optimal of 32.0 km and 40.1 minutes, POL-RD-02 gives ((3.80 + 0.75 x 32.0 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 = 39.828. Charged total 43.41 - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is above the 0.50 de minimis and below 90% of the charge, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND.

CLAIMS THAT CHANGE NOTHING. POL-RD-04 does not rescue the driver or bind the rider: the chat log shows the driver proposing the diversion ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok') and the rider merely replying 'ok but not too long ah'. The rider named no place or road and waypoint_hint is null, so no rider-requested-detour exoneration exists. POL-RD-09 adds nothing — no ERP gantries, tolls, surcharge or phantom line to correct. POL-RD-10 is not engaged: identifiers match across the three core artifacts, the trace is unimpaired, and the refund is far below the escalation threshold. No referral arises either: POL-RD-06(c) needs a repeat-deviation pattern, and the driver's profile shows 1 flag in 288 completed trips, far below the clause's thresholds; POL-RD-09(4) needs an unmatched charge line, and there is none.

IMPAIRED ARTIFACT. EV-ADVIS-00104-02 (the CTE breakdown advisory) is impaired at weight 0.25 with issue codes ADVISORY_UNCORROBORATED and UNVERIFIED_SOURCE. It carries no deciding fact on this trip — its geometry covers a corridor the trace never enters — so, per POL-GEN-02(2), it does not cap the confidence of any finding here, and it is left out of account.

The decision rests on EV-GPS-00104, EV-TRIP-00104, EV-FARE-00104 and EV-ADVIS-00104-01, all at weight 1.0; confidence is 0.90.
